identity.name: Fortune Website Guide multi-turn retrieval evaluation

charter.decision: Determine whether the deployed guide can sustain source-grounded retrieval across longer conversations without losing the latest topic, reviving stale topics, inventing facts, or becoming verbose.
charter.unitUnderTest: The deployed Website Guide system, including sequential API state, the three-exchange client history window, retrieval routing, approved-source validation, deterministic answers, and model-backed source selection.
charter.targetPopulation: Public visitors asking English or Spanish follow-up questions about device programs, classes, learning resources, individual support, certifications, schedules, registration, and the Digital Equity Program.
charter.minimumPracticalDifference: One failed hard episode, a ten-point change in required episode success, or a fifteen-point change in deictic and topic-shift turn success.
hardConstraints: Every source and related link stays on the approved Fortune host.
The conversation ID remains stable within an episode.
The first turn is opening and later turns are follow-up.
Production capture remains none and the evaluator remains disabled.
A topic shift cannot revive a source from an older topic.
nonGoals: Evaluate the quality of Fortune services.
Replace Fortune staff review of facts, Spanish, tone, or participant comprehension.
Rank the foundation model independently from the retrieval system.

coverage.historyWindow: The latest three user-assistant exchanges, matching the published browser client.
coverage.hiddenTestAccess: A Fortune-owned holdout remains future work; this regression suite is reviewable and versioned.

state: Reuse the API conversation ID returned by the first turn.
Reuse the continuation token only when the deployment returns one.
Send no more than the latest six safe history messages.
Use a fresh client event ID for every turn.

graders.adjudication: Manually inspect every failed semantic turn against the approved source record before changing an expectation.
A named Fortune source owner resolves factual and routing disputes.

primary.unit: proportion of required episodes passing every turn

diagnostics: deictic, elliptical, and topic-shift turn success
metrics.uncertainty: Wilson 95 percent interval over required episodes; turns within an episode are not treated as independent samples.

analysis.uncertainty: Wilson 95 percent interval over required episodes.
analysis.missingDataRule: A missing, malformed, timed-out, or exhausted turn fails its episode.
analysis.stoppingRule: Run every frozen episode unless a privacy boundary fails or a shared rate limit is reached.

releaseGates: At least 10 episodes and 40 total turns complete.
At least 90 percent of required episodes pass.
At least 85 percent of contextual turns pass.
Every multi-episode slice passes at least 75 percent.
